name: room
text: Room opened — goal: mining: Gather AI info from DIVERSE sources (GitHub/HN/Product Hunt/Reddit/Telegram/social), NOT j

name: Pick
text: I’ll fire up the mining pipeline: target GitHub’s trending AI repos (last 30 days, >100 stars) and scrape HN’s “Show HN” AI posts (top 50). Commands: `gh search repos --q "ai" --sort stars --order desc --created ">2024-05-01" --json name,url,stars > github_ai.json` and `curl -s "https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search?query=ai&tags=show_hn&hitsPerPage=50" | jq '.hits[] | {title,url,points}' > hn_ai.json`. Files will land in `/data/mined/`; next, I’ll parse and deduplicate before feeding to the lead.

name: Assay
text: Assay: Hold—your GitHub scrape is too narrow. You’re filtering for *created* after May 1st, but "trending" implies *activity*, not just birthdate. Where’s the evidence that new repos (>100 stars in 30 days) correlate with *current* relevance? And HN’s "Show HN" top 50? That’s a popularity contest, not a signal of *diverse* or *quality* sources—where’s the risk of echo chambers or low-signal noise? Show me the failure modes.
